data.title: RenovoRx regains Nasdaq compliance
data.description:
RenovoRx (RNXT) announced on Friday that it has received a Nasdaq notification, confirming that the company has regained compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

The Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff notified RenovoRx that the closing bid price of its common stock was at $1.00 per share or greater for the 10 consecutive business days from August 6, 2026, through August 19, 2026. Accordingly, RenovoRx has regained compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), and Nasdaq has confirmed that the matter is now closed. 

The notification has no effect on the trading of the company’s common stock, which continues to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol “RNXT.”

Source: press release

data.title: RenX Enterprises to sell Georgia property for $2.6M to reduce debt
data.description:
• RenX Enterprises (RENX) announced on Friday that its 50%-owned JV agreed to sell a 7.7-acre Georgia property for $2.6M.
  • About $800K of the sale proceeds is expected to repay two notes held by the company, with the remaining proceeds split between the joint venture partners.
  • The company expects to receive about $900K from the remaining proceeds and use the funds to support its Myakka City, Florida, operations.
  • It is preparing to commission its Microtec milling system in the second half of 2026.
  • CEO David Villarreal said the sale supports the company’s strategy of monetizing legacy real estate, reducing debt, and investing in its core operations.
  • Closing remains subject to customary conditions, including due diligence, state program approvals, and financing.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: BofA Securities flags contrarian trades across bonds, China, dollar, AI and U.S. midterms
data.description:
BofA Securities is highlighting a series of “anti-consensus” trades that it believes could outperform as some of the market’s most entrenched investment narratives begin to lose steam.

The bank’s contrarian ideas span bonds, China, the U.S. dollar, artificial intelligence and the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, with several trades designed to benefit from a reversal in prevailing investor positioning.

In its contrarian “ABB” trade, BofA Securities is pushing back against the “Anything But Bonds” consensus. The bank favors unloved, long-duration assets including real estate investment trusts (REITs), the XBI biotechnology ETF, the KRE regional banking ETF and small-cap stocks.

BofA argues that another significant leg higher in bond yields would become increasingly damaging to both Wall Street and the broader U.S. economy, potentially forcing policymakers to intervene. That prospect, in its view, could create an environment in which long-duration assets regain favor.

The bank’s “ABC” trade takes aim at the long-standing “Anywhere But China” narrative. BofA Securities is bullish on Hong Kong’s property sector, arguing that two of the major bearish themes of the 2020s, Chinese assets and real estate, could be approaching an inflection point. A stabilization or recovery in China’s property market could therefore offer an opportunity in an area that has remained deeply out of favor with global investors.

BofA’s “ABD” trade acknowledges the broad “Anything But the Dollar” sentiment but argues that gold remains the cleanest way to express the view of continued dollar debasement, asset inflation and potential bond-market stress.

The bank also points to the changing political dynamics of the 2020s and U.S.-Iran “economic warfare” as factors that could support gold through increased demand for sanctions protection and safe-haven assets.

On artificial intelligence, BofA takes a more nuanced contrarian position. While the secular consensus remains firmly bullish on AI stocks, the bank recommends investors consider a “short AI bonds” approach, arguing that even if the U.S. government can influence or cap yields, a meaningful reduction in the cost of capital would likely require deflation or a recession.

At the same time, BofA recommends barbell exposure around AI equities by adding commodities and natural-resource companies that stand to benefit from the enormous energy and materials requirements of the AI arms race between the U.S. and China.

BofA Securities is also positioning for a potentially more disruptive outcome from the November U.S. midterm elections. While consensus expectations do not point to a Democratic sweep, the bank recommends hedging that scenario through short exposure to financial stocks.

If Democrats were to take the Senate while Republicans also lose the Texas governor’s mansion, BofA sees the possibility of a greater than 10% decline in stocks, accompanied by weakness in the U.S. dollar and bond yields into year-end.

The bank points to President Donald Trump’s approval ratings, 39% overall, 36% on the economy and 30% on inflation, as being well below pre-war averages of 46%, 42% and 38%, respectively, suggesting political risks could become increasingly important for markets as the midterms approach.

data.title: Trump opens beef imports for 90 days in bid to tame record prices
data.description:
President Trump is giving beef eaters a reprieve from high prices by lifting the import quotas on imported ground beef for 90 days.

In a social media post, Trump said the U.S. would allow 300K metric tons of ground beef to be brought into the U.S. without paying import tariffs with a “commitment” that it would be sold at 25% below current market prices. The president did not specify where the beef was being imported from, but according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture ((USDA)) the majority of beef imported into the U.S. comes from Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Mexico.

The tariff holiday will make consumers and foreign beef providers happy but will likely face opposition from domestic ranchers who continue to struggle with a 75-year low in the U.S. cattle herd due to a severe drought in the Great Plains and Western states, increased feed costs, and cattle import restrictions from Mexico due to the New World screwworm.  

With the U.S. cattle herd at multi-generational lows, the White House sought to protect domestic ranchers and curb what it called the “foreign-dominated conglomerates that control America’s meat supply” by imposing a 26.4% tariff on over-quota beef imports (imports within the quota face a much lower tariff of $0.044 per kilogram). At the same time, the USDA took steps to rebuild the domestic herd, including expanding grazing on federal lands and limiting the “Product of the USA” label to beef from cattle born, raised, and slaughtered in the U.S.

Since this did little to address the challenges faced by domestic slaughterhouses and meatpacking/processing plants, the Administration lowered the tariff and allowed significantly more beef to come into the U.S. from Argentina under the “Ensuring Affordable Beef for the American Consumer” executive order.  

Unfortunately, Trump’s executive order failed to stop the meteoric increase in the price of beef. Prices dipped slightly in the wake of the E.O. before resuming their advance, reaching a record of $6.89 for a pound of ground beef last month.

Trump’s proposal to increase meat imports is weighing on shares of Tyson Foods (TSN) one of the "Big Four" meat producers, while at the same time, shares of Brazil-based JBS N.V. (JBS) are trending higher into the open.

data.title: Japan ends 4-year crypto approval freeze with Nomura-backed Laser Digital
data.description:
Japan’s digital asset market is opening a new chapter as Nomura-backed Laser Digital Japan secures regulatory approval, ending a four-year gap in new crypto asset exchange registrations and creating a fresh institutional gateway into the market.

Laser Digital Japan, the Japanese entity of Nomura (NMR)'s digital assets subsidiary Laser Digital, announced on Friday that it had completed registration as a "crypto asset exchange service provider" under Japan’s Payment Services Act.

The approval comes as Japanese institutional investors show growing interest in digital assets. A 2026 'Institutional Investor Survey' published by Nomura and Laser Digital found that 65% of respondents see crypto assets as an opportunity to diversify portfolios, while nearly 79% of those investors plan to invest in digital assets over the next three years.

According to the official release, the company will initially focus on providing liquidity to local virtual asset service providers. It also plans to eventually offer digital asset trading services to institutional investors, although the company has not yet announced when those services will launch.

The timing also comes after the country introduced major crypto-related regulatory reforms, including rules covering stablecoins. It also gives institutional investors another regulated route into the digital asset market.

For Laser Digital Japan, the immediate focus remains compliance, risk management, and building institutional-grade infrastructure in the country. The company said further details on its services will be announced later.

While the announcement does not directly reference crypto stocks, the move could be positive for names such as Metaplanet (MTPLF), Coinbase Global (COIN), Circle Internet Group (CRCL), Strategy (MSTR), and Galaxy Digital (GLXY), as clearer regulation and rising institutional demand could support broader digital asset market trends.

data.title: Morgan Stanley said to pick Dallas for expansion outside NYC
data.description:
Morgan Stanley (MS) plans to relocate up to 4,800 jobs to the Texas city, passing over Alpharetta, Georgia, for the expansion, according to a media report.

The Wall Street giant will anchor a new $1.3B, 709K-square-foot office tower in Dallas, the New York Post reported, citing municipal filings. The company plans to bring up to 4,800 jobs to the state by 2031.

It was previously reported that Morgan Stanley (MS) had narrowed down potential expansion sites to Dallas and Alpharetta, Georgia. In June, the Dallas City Council approved $18.5M in economic development grants for the project. Furthermore, the city determined that it qualifies for tax relief and other incentives, including up to 10 years of property tax abatements.

The expansion will occur in two phases. Initially, the bank will occupy 255K square feet at Fountain Place, on 1445 Ross Ave. in downtown Dallas, which will undergo a $97M interior renovation. Eventually, the bank's workers will move to the new $1.3B skyscraper at 2401 McKinney Ave., the NY Post said.

Morgan Stanley (MS) did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

For years, Wall Street's biggest banks and financial firms have been expanding to more affordable regions that are friendlier to businesses. The rhetoric has increased since Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Apollo Global Management (APO), and Goldman Sachs (GS) have also moved jobs to Dallas.

Hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin has threatened to halt a major expansion of his Citadel firm due to the new mayor's proposed tax policies. However, earlier this month, an affiliate of Griffin's entered a joint venture with Vornado Realty (VNO) to develop a 1.9M-square-foot trophy building on Park Avenue, where Citadel will enter a 15-year lease on 1.05M square feet of space.

data.title: UBS lifts S&P 500 target to 8,100 despite recent slide
data.description:
UBS has lifted its year-end 2026 S&P 500 (SP500) target to 8,100 and its mid-2027 forecast to 8,400, signaling continued confidence in the equity bull market despite a recent pullback that left the benchmark hovering near 7,641.

The revised targets imply roughly 6% upside by December and about 10% by next June from current levels. Underlying the more constructive outlook are stronger earnings expectations: the bank now projects S&P 500 earnings per share of $350 in 2026 and $400 in 2027. Growth is expected to be led by technology, semiconductors, and energy. 

UBS cites three primary supports for its bullish stance—resilient U.S. economic expansion, a patient Federal Reserve, and accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence.

At the same time, the firm flags several risks that could challenge the advance, including higher oil prices, a potential reacceleration of inflation, and the possibility that AI investments fail to deliver the anticipated returns.
